about: A rewrite of the tar archive tool in Rust, aiming to work the same as GNU tar.

prs.title: Archives with read-only folders now extract
prs.broken: tar created a read-only folder with its final permissions before the files inside it, so writing those files failed and extraction stopped. GNU tar extracts them.
prs.changed: Folders now get their permissions after everything inside them is written, deepest folders first.
prs.matters: Archives of read-only folders unpack the same way they do with GNU tar.

prs.title: Archive listings now show link targets and local times
prs.broken: The verbose archive listing printed times in UTC, showed a hard link as an empty file, and left out where links point. GNU tar shows local time and the link targets.
prs.changed: Listings now use the local time zone, mark hard links, and print the target of every link the way GNU tar does.
prs.matters: People reading a listing see the same thing they would with GNU tar.

prs.title: Extracting absolute paths now says so
prs.broken: Archives with absolute paths were quietly extracted under the current folder, with no note that the leading slash was removed.
prs.changed: Extraction now prints the same warning as GNU tar, once for each different prefix.
prs.matters: People can see that files landed somewhere other than the path stored in the archive.
